questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Limit at Positive or Negative Infinity Using L'Hopital's Rule
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, we have an indeterminate form of type $\frac{\infty }{\infty },$ so applying  L'Hopital's rule yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{e}^{x}} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{[2\operatorname{ln}⁡x]}^{′}}{[{e}^{x}]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2}{x})}{{e}^{x}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2}{x{e}^{x}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Indeterminate Limit of the Form Infinity Divided by Infinity Using L'Hopital's Rule
questions.worked_solution:
Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{-\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{\operatorname{csc}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)]}^{′}}{[\operatorname{csc}⁡x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}}{\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cancel{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡x} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Limit Using L'Hopital's Rule Twice
questions.worked_solution:
If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x{e}^{2x}-x+3{x}^{2}}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{[x{e}^{2x}-x+3{x}^{2}]^{′}}{[{sin}^{2}⁡x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(1+2x){e}^{2x}-1+6x}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(1+2x){e}^{2x}-1+6x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x{e}^{2x}-x+3{x}^{2}}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(1+2x){e}^{2x}-1+6x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{[(1+2x){e}^{2x}-1+6x]^{′}}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡2x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(4+4x){e}^{2x}+6}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{(4+0){e}^{0}+6}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡0} \\  & =\frac{4+6}{2} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Limit Using L'Hopital's Rule Twice
questions.worked_solution:
If we plug in $x=3$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{({x}^{2}-5)^{2}-48x+128}{{x}^{2}-6x+9} & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{{[({x}^{2}-5)^{2}-48x+128]}^{′}}{[{x}^{2}-6x+9]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{4x({x}^{2}-5)-48}{2x-6} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{2{x}^{3}-10x-24}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{({x}^{2}-5)^{2}-48x+128}{{x}^{2}-6x+9} & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{2{x}^{3}-10x-24}{x-3} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{{[2{x}^{3}-10x-24]}^{′}}{{[x-3]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{6{x}^{2}-10}{1} \\  & =6(3)^{2}-10 \\  & =44.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Limit at Positive or Negative Infinity Using L'Hopital's Rule
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, we have an indeterminate form of type $\frac{\infty }{\infty },$ so applying L'Hopital's rule yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+9x-4}{3x+1} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+9x-4]^{′}}{[3x+1]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2}{x}+9)}{3} \\  & =\frac{0+9}{3} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
